Researching the decay $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ to determine how it relates to the theory of minimal electroweak symmetry breaking, specifically through the diagram with a box shape, requires a precise understanding of the amplitude's phase information. A current issue in experimental physics is the need to verify or discredit this type of di-boson contribution. By increasing the sensitivity of the decay rate's amplitude and its phase to variation in several relevant parameters, our analysis offers potential lines of investigation for the particle physics experiment LHCb at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. Or, in the case of certain recent results, it leads to disagreement with the existing data. In the process, our research identifies three observable quantities whose values are currently critical in distinguishing between different theoretical predictions. In the context of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay, we also highlight the significance of investigating the $B^0\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay as a complementary approach.

This paper presents a numerical analysis of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with a nonuniform mesh. We first establish the convergence of a discrete control problem to its continuous counterpart. We then examine the optimal policy of the discrete problem and provide an estimate of its convergence rate. The study assumes the coefficient of the parabolic equation is known and meets certain smoothness criteria. We achieve the analysis by applying a variety of techniques, including the Green's function, stochastic monotonicity, and the Browder-Minty lemma.

The observed variation in ultra-high energy cosmic ray arrival directions exceeds expectations from local magnetic field instabilities alone. To further investigate this discrepancy, we analyzed x-ray flares from 963 active galaxies and 69 blazars over 12.5 years, and found no correlation with cosmic ray arrival directions. We subsequently detected an excess of cosmic rays at the highest energies and in the largest flux increments, with rates 3.5 to 4.5 standard deviations above predictions. This discrepancy cannot be attributed to any known astrophysical phenomenon and its significance varies based on the cosmic ray energy and nearby nearby X-ray flares.

The ATLAS collaboration within the LHC, utilizes its sophisticated detector system to examine p+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV, enabling a detailed investigation of p+p collisions up to 2.76 TeV. Through a comprehensive study, the anti-$p$/$p$ and nuclear modification factor $A_{\rm NP}$ spectra have been accurately determined for various charged hadrons ranging from 0.3 to 400 GeV in central p+Pb collisions. The analysis reveals an apparent discrepancy between current theoretical models and experimental data, prompting further investigation into possible uncertainties in theoretical predictions, alternative explanations, and the consistency with previously published results at lower energies.

This work delves into the realm of noncommutative quantum mechanics, specifically exploring its underlying principles and the role of Lie algebras within this context. Our discussion also touches on a previously underrepresented topic, deformed Hamiltonian systems.

Invasive tumor infiltrating lymphocytes play a significant role in a patient's cancer prognosis, and their quantification within H&E histology images is crucial. AI-based approaches have been explored for automatically categorizing lymphocytes based on their invasion depth into tumor tissues. However, these methods are constrained by the need for large-scale, high-quality training datasets, which are difficult to assemble due to the time-consuming and subjective nature of lymphocyte annotation. In this study, we integrate federated learning with a novel, efficient data annotation process called "crowd-labeled networks" to develop a lightweight, reliable, and transferable model for predicting lymphocytes based on their invasion level. Notably, our technique avoids exchanging sensitive medical data across institutions and eliminates the need for comprehensive training datasets. The results of this research demonstrate the potential of federated learning to accurately identify invading lymphocytes with minimal access to annotated tissue samples.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s using the on-off keying technique, over a distance of 18.8km in a South China Sea submarine cable that lacks dispersion compensation. Analysis and field trials reveal the limitations of the four-stage decision-feedback equalizer in handling burst errors, resulting in reduced signal quality and data transfer errors. To address this challenge, a modified version of the DFE is proposed, effectively mitigating burst-error propagation and significantly improving transmission performance.

Temporal convolutional networks have been widely adopted for their ability to process time series data outside of a sequential context. However, their success is hindered by the limited size of available training data, due to the high computational cost of convolutional network-based methods. To overcome this challenge, researchers often turn to trimming and sampling techniques, but these methods can distort the data's original temporal structure. In contrast, our proposed trimming in time (PIT) network framework optimizer successfully balances the need for longer temporal dynamics capture against the limitation of available data. By utilizing interpolation and the optimal network trimming strategy, PIT enables the efficient exploration of limited data sets. Our experiments demonstrate that PIT outperforms the baseline method, particularly notable in the MIMIC-III database, where a 22% improvement in performance was achieved on the telaboratory dataset.

This paper proves that any variety of linear algebras containing at least one 3-generator 3-dimensional member, excludes the family of basic Lie algebras. The excluded algebras are: one-dimensional, two-dimensional, Heisenberg algebras and bivector algebras in three dimensions. It is also shown that the variety of Lie algebras defined by five-dimensional filiform solvable algebras bases is equal to the variety of  one-dimensional algebras.

Our study delves into the observation of stream angle fluctuations in lead-lead collisions at a 5.02 TeV collision energy. Measuring these fluctuations, along with those of flow intensity, as a function of the stream angle in each hemisphere, allows us to investigate the balance of particle and antiparticle flows and any possible dependence on the quark content of the final-state particles. Based on data collected by the ALICE detector at the LHC, our results demonstrate that fluctuations are unaffected by the stream angle and reveal an asymmetry in the ratio of particle to antiparticle flow, which becomes more pronounced in more central collisions; this trend is consistent with theoretical predictions arising from the interplay between the imaginary part of the polarized self-energy and chiral-dynamical susceptibility in the medium.

The unified correspondence theory in the context of DLE-Logics leverages the symmetry of interpretation to reverse the order of the correspondence, achieving a bidirectional understanding of how models and formulas relate. Additionally, this approach facilitates a common framework that encompasses diverse theories within DLE-Logics, including modal logic, modal logic with propositional multiplicity, and fuzzy logic using distribution functions.

Information stewards encounter a challenging problem when attempting to integrate tables with missing values and functional dependencies. Current solutions that handle missing values, such as those based on information-theoretic approaches or matching tables with identical column names, are insufficient to tackle this broader integration issue. Stewards require methods that can handle the complexities of nulls and functional dependencies when integrating tables, and this paper presents an innovative approach using the Henkin repair theorem to generate consistent tables. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by describing a practical algorithm capable of handling a specific instance of this problem, and we also explore the challenge of defining a functional dependency language that can be used for integration purposes.

This study presents a novel temporal-variance Poisson autoregressive model called TVPAR($p,q$) that incorporates time-dependent conditional variance for countable data series. Our model is an adaptation of the GJR-GARCH model, incorporating the time-variance component, which is linked to historical shock values. We demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of the TVPAR($p,q$) model, as well as its asymptotic properties. Specifically, we show that the consistent maximum likelihood estimator can recover the true parameters and root $T^0 in the asymptotic distribution. Moreover, a simulation experiment is designed to evaluate the performance of the maximum likelihood estimator under specific data settings. Notably, TVPAR($p,q$) outperforms its competitors in terms of mean squared error in various scenarios.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object poses and shapes, with the ability to adapt to changing
lighting conditions. This representation is based on a descriptor field, which
is a function that identifies whether two points are on the object in question,
and is employed in a maximum likelihood estimation framework to predict the
object's pose, shape, and lighting. In practice, this means positing a set of
pose hypotheses and calculating the likelihood of each one being correct, with
the actual pose being the one with the highest likelihood. We've found that this
method excels at handling real-world noise and variability, and that it's quite
efficient in terms of both training and inference times. We've also found that
NDFs are highly adaptable to different types of objects and are easy to
extend to multiple objects. Additionally, they support robust grasping, with
which we mean that they can find a stable pose for each object and calculate a
stable set of poses for all objects at once.

The SiD detector is one of the two conceptual detectors designed for the future ILC, specifically tailored to precisely identify electrons and Higgs bosons while providing effective probe capabilities for dark matter and neutrino research. As the silicon vertex and tracking system within SiD features a novel 3D silicon sensor design, we are reviewing the underlying principles of this design, including the underlying physics, design aims, and R&D activities. Furthermore, we are reviewing the status of the 3D silicon sensor development, possible suppression methods for electron hits, and the feasibility of using such sensors in the forward detector region.

We performed the first in-depth analysis of seven red giant members in the globular cluster Tononzintla 2. We were able to estimate the cluster's distance at 11.75 ± 1.45 Mpc and a relative age of 12.3 ± 1.5 seconds in the age-scale of Baumgardt. Notably, this makes the cluster significantly younger than the nearby globular cluster M31-T7. Additionally, the estimation of the total luminosity of the cluster at its distance allows us to calculate its total mass, which is in the range of (4.3-6.8) x 10^5 solar masses, and when considering the fraction of luminous stars in the cluster, the mass falls between (2.0-3.1) x 10^5 solar masses.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP) serves as an extensive collection of formal proofs developed using the Isabelle proof assistant. With over 1000 contributions and growing, maintaining an overview of developed theories becomes increasingly difficult. This difficulty presents a significant challenge for users in tracking changes, locating specific content, and conducting in-depth analyses of the archive. Our project involves assessing and refining the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs using a custom-developed set of tools and verification frameworks. These tools comprise a variant of the Isabelle evaluator and a theorem verifier based on the Lean 3.0 proof assistant. This evaluation provides valuable insights into enhancing the archive's usability and content.

Using the functional renormalization group at the edge of the Yang-Lee domain, where a classical O(N) symmetric system undergoes a transition from analyticity, we determine the position of the singularity for all O(N) universality classes. This occurs when the temperature is close to its critical value and the imaginary part of the susceptibility becomes singular, typically indicating a phase transition. Our study finds that in 2D, this singularity is more strongly temperature-dependent than in higher dimensions, with the critical exponent shifting from $-\frac{1}{2}$ in 2D to $-1$ in higher dimensions and beyond. We also derive a precise formula for the singularity in 4D and higher dimensions, which can be used as a more accurate predictor for critical temperatures than existing universal relations in models like the O(4) ferromagnet.

In statistical mechanics, thedreamt-of variational principle by Parisi can be achieved through a minimax formulation involving the replica model's mean field theory (MFT) and a nonconvex objective function. Post-AMP (Approximate Message Passing) minimization of this formulation has been extensively analyzed, yet a fundamental aspect of the approach remains unexplored. We have obtained an expression for the gap between the post-AMP solution and an MFT-based upper bound on the replica model's objective function. This difference is characterized by a convex function that upper bounds the original nonconvex function. As a consequence of this relationship, we can determine the convexity of the post-AMP solution by examining a simpler function related to an MFT-based perspective. Additionally, this result implies the local concavity of the TAP free energy at an optimal solution.

Recent advancements in radio frequency and microwave technology have been driven by the development of low-frequency metaelectrics and acoustic metasurfaces. These advanced technologies enable innovative applications such as invisible antennas and cloaking devices. This paper delves into the fundamental science behind these breakthroughs, focusing on the interrelationship between structure, composition, and functional behavior within metasurfaces. By combining theoretical modeling and numerical simulation, our research offers an in-depth analysis of electromagnetic-matter interactions at the microscale, offering insight into the complex dynamics that give rise to electromagnetic phenomena. This comprehensive understanding, made possible by our study, provides a strong foundation for the design of next-generation communication technologies.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth fully integrable vector fields near a hyperbolic singularity. The theorem of linearization around a non-degenerate critical point is well-known in the smooth category. However, the same cannot be directly applied to a degenerate critical point due to the absence of the Hartman-Guillemin theorem's conclusion. The main contribution of this study is the demonstration that smooth fully integrable vector fields possess a locally orbital linearizing coordinate transformation. The key step in the proof involves the construction of a smooth coordinate change that normalizes the first Lyapunov coordinate, followed by an application of the Hartman-Guillemin theorem to the resulting vector field.

This paper proposes a deep learning approach known as the Configuration Interaction Potential Network (CI-PNet) to predict the full potential energy surface of electrons in atoms and molecules from scratch. Building on previous work with single-electron potential networks, this model integrates multiple electrons through a configuration interaction transformation, enabling the description of electronic interactions and facilitating the interpretation of the results in terms of wave function components. In experiments, the proposed CI-PNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in benchmarking potential energy surfaces for specific atoms and molecules and effectively identifies reaction pathways and critical points on potential energy landscapes.

A remarkable alignment of nine blazars at extremely high redshifts ($z>0.5$) has been observed, exhibiting a distinct arc shape on the celestial map. Furthermore, their distribution exhibits a substantial curve, observed only once before in Fornax, a region in the sky. This unusual pattern's statistical significance is 3.5 sigma. It's essential to note that the association of these blazars was based on their radio and optical properties and was identified through a robotic system. The findings suggest that these high-redshift blazars represent a previously undetected population and are likely to have significant effects on high-redshift cosmic surveys.

The use of photometry from space-based telescopes, specifically using stellar light, enables the non-invasive monitoring of aerosol levels. This method has seen significant development in the last decade, offering promising possibilities for wide-scale and long-term observations of aerosols in multiple wavelength ranges. Despite some limitations, such as the influence of local site conditions and how they affect measurements, these techniques have yielded outstanding results, including the recovery of historical data with a precision of less than 5 microns and the accurate measurement of the spatial variability of aerosols with resolutions as fine as 300 meters. These advancements open up exciting prospects for the simultaneous monitoring of aerosols and stellar light across the entire visible spectrum using low-cost filters and a wide range of stellar sources, which could provide valuable information for a wide range of applications, including climate science, urban planning and the optimization of astronomical observations.

Recently, estimating a 3D object's pose using only an object's 2D image has become a major focus in computer vision research. This process, known as single-view 3D pose estimation or 6DoF pose estimation, can be critical in applications like autonomous driving, robotics, and video game development. One widely used approach to this problem involves using a neural network to directly predict a 3D rotation and translation vector from a 2D image. Another approach, often employed in traditional computer vision methods, involves first creating 2D feature correspondences between the image and a 3D object model, and then using these correspondences to estimate the pose. Our research suggests that these two methods can be more effective when combined. We present a new model, called DeepHMap++, which integrates these two strategies by using a neural network to first create a comprehensive list of potential 2D-3D feature matches, and then selects the most appropriate subset of these matches to estimate the pose. In our experiments, we show that our proposed model outperforms direct prediction methods, while also demonstrating that DeepHMap++'s performance can be further improved by adding a correspondence filter module, and that this approach is also robust in real-world scenarios.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, delivering a comprehensive framework that incorporates nonlocal effects and bridges the gap between continuum and particle-based methods. This review paper delves into the development and use of bond-based peridynamics, discussing both its fundamental concepts and various practical implementations, as well as examining the potential applications of peridynamic theory to fluid dynamics. Key concepts in peridynamics are initially explained, including nonlocal kernels and junction conditions, which are then explored in detail. The review then explores numerical approaches to solving PD equations, presenting both traditional methods and more recent algorithms before considering the potential benefits of adopting a peridynamic approach in fluid dynamics, even including a basic introduction to PD models for fluids.

We present GGLasso, a Python tool using the ARMA4J Python package, for resolving Large Scale Sparse Graphical Lasso problems. Our implementation builds on the success of Cholesky Based Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers, and through computational testing on various datasets, demonstrates its capability to handle large scale and sparse problems. Additionally, GGLasso is an open source and user friendly library, offering a simple and intuitive API for solving Generalized Graphical Lasso problems.

Numerous numerical methods in molecular science rely on sampling configurational space. A novel approach modifies the classic Langevin Dynamics method to efficiently and effectively minimize bias in calculating thermodynamic averages. The Hamming distance metric is used to assess configurational space coverage, and our optimization strategy consistently produces superior results for a challenging set of test systems. Another significant benefit of this approach is that it generates an order of magnitude fewer conformers compared to common methods like MMVB, making it extremely well-suited for handling large biomolecules.

We performed a suite of highly accurate simulations for the merger of two medium-sized black holes in various environments, including both Einstein's general theory of relativity and a cosmological model with dark energy. These simulations were conducted to quantify potential systematic errors in theoretical models of gravitational waves when based on a specific dark energy cosmology. Our findings suggest that even high-resolution numerical processes may be susceptible to minor artificial distortions when modeling the densest regions of merging black holes. Nonetheless, our study confirms that any discrepancies arising from these processes have negligible impact on the characteristic frequencies of gravitational waves emitted during black hole collisions. Furthermore, our research provides a precise basis for comparing theoretical models of gravitational waves against their observed counterparts, and such studies can be expanded to include a broader range of black hole collision scenarios.

We have analyzed the Euler-Bernoulli beam equation on a rotating star-shaped graph for its stability and non-palability properties. A key inequality involving the first eigenvalue and a specific function of the curvature has been established. Furthermore, we have determined the conditions under which the solution space does not contain a path for which the Euler-Bernoulli functional attains its minimum. Additionally, we have found that the first eigenvalue plays a crucial role in establishing the stability of the system. A stability inequality has been derived, along with a specific inequality applicable when the graph is symmetric. A numerical method for computing the first eigenvalue and a corresponding eigenfunction has been proposed. This method relies on an iterative process involving the finite element method. A numerical example illustrating the convergence of this method has been provided.

Our novel acoustic lens substance is proposed to significantly expand the detection capabilities of photoacoustic imaging. By altering an acoustic lens's characteristics, we successfully demonstrate the potential to the extend the detection region to more than two times the distance from the sensor axis. The optimization technique we use, based on the collimation principle, is straightforward and readily applicable to various acoustic lens designs. However, the most surprising benefit of this approach is the substantial reduction of peak lateral displacement, from 2.5 to 0.14, which greatly eases the reconstruction of 3D images. We have successfully tested our acoustic lens and the imaging technique on phantom tissue mimics and real breast tissue. The results show a notable improvement in detected lesion sizes and a significant reduction in the side-lobes effect, which is a major limitation in photoacoustic imaging.

The concept of eigenvector centrality in network analysis provides a local measure that effectively identifies crucial nodes. We present a multi-layer eigenvector approach that incorporates varying levels of node significance across different network layers. This generalised centrality framework can be applied to specific analysis contexts by adapting relevant significance relationships. Notably, the proposed method offers a significant enhancement over existing approaches by incorporating relationships between node significances across different network layers, enabling the identification of influential nodes with a broader perspective.

We tackle the problem of non-blind and weakly-supervised raw image restoration, 
which involves demosaicking, deblurring and denoising raw images based on partially 
collected and underexposed images. By analyzing the raw image formation model, we 
establish a physical-based raw image restoration model that integrates the effects 
of image blurring, photon counting and sensor sensitivity. We then propose a novel 
and highly flexible raw image restoration model that comprises a physical-based forward 
operator and a traditional inverse problem solver. To tackle the computational 
challenge, we introduce an end-to-end deep collaborative model that divides the task 
into demosaicking, deblurring and denoising components and leverages shared features. 
By leveraging shared structures and taking adaptability into account, we propose a 
flexible and overcomplete multi-resolution framework that is capable of solving this 
highly complex inverse problem. We evaluate our proposed model and compare it to 
state-of-the-art baselines using a newly collected and publicly available raw image 
dataset, and the experimental results show significant improvements in quality and 
perceptual metrics.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

Introducing the Causal Exploration Toolbox (CET), a free and open-source
collection of causal inference methods for Python. This suite of tools is
designed to aid researchers in uncovering the underlying causal structures of
their data. Based on the implementation of established algorithms, CET offers
a versatile and user-friendly platform for conducting causal investigations.

Research into the seal performance of spheres moving through a fluid at high speeds has been the subject of prior studies. This research extends that understanding by exploring the seal dynamics of spheres entering a fluid at moderate speeds, where both viscous and inertial forces significantly impact the surrounding fluid. A theoretical analysis was conducted to model the growth of the water sphere around the entering sphere, with results showing that a critical speed exists above which the water sphere formation becomes unstable. Experimental testing of this concept was performed using a high-speed camera and pressure sensors, and the findings align with the results of the theoretical analysis, including the existence of a critical speed threshold. Moreover, the data suggest that when the sphere moves at a speed greater than twice its diameter, the pressure distribution around it becomes steady and similar to that of a stationary sphere.

We investigate a class of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories characterized by an enlarged S.O(2) global symmetry. The presence of this additional symmetry restricts the possible low-energy interactions through its application of R-R charge conservation. In line with established conservation laws, we derive a set of constraints and classify the possible scalar and axion monodromy 3-torsions that maintain the global symmetry. Furthermore, we establish that the extended theta-term is minimal and can be expressed as a combination of the individual theta-terms associated with each R-R charge conservation constraint.

This text cannot be called confidential information because it has already been publicly disclosed through at least one earlier publication. Nonetheless, we will maintain the customary practice in research of referring to prior works in a limited manner. Recently, researchers demonstrated the potential for side-channel attacks on hardware to expose sensitive information, leading some to advocate for implementing hardware-based isolation to protect against such breaches. In response, our study explored the feasibility of conducting an acoustic side-channel attack. We discovered that an external microphone can pick up the audio emitted by a computer's speaker, allowing it to infer the password entered on that computer. This finding was independently verified by additional researchers. We also examined various methods for mitigating this type of attack, including the use of noise to mask the sound emitted by the speaker and the selection of a password based on the output of a speech system. We selected our project to serve as a representative example of the kind of research enabled by the newly established Acoustic Side-Channel Attack (ASCA) testbed, which provides a framework for conducting and comparing the security risks associated with different hardware configurations.

Reinforcement learning (RL) is vulnerable to significant corruption of its reward signal, which hinders its application to high-risk fields. This challenge stems from the fact that RL algorithms typically rely on the expected return value and suffer from a fundamental limitation in estimating the gradient of the expected return. In this paper, we introduce an innovative approach based on the exploration-exploitation trade-off, which derives a corrupted return estimate that can be used to optimize an robust policy. This framework is theoretically backed by the guarantee that the proposed algorithm achieves optimal exploration-exploitation results in finite horizons. Moreover, our algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art RL methods in various challenging scenarios evaluated using a range of games and simulations.

In our previous study, we observed quasiperiodic behavior in the classic box game model, where players are not required to make distinct choices. This phenomenon was demonstrated through numerical simulations and analytical methods, revealing that the model exhibits a persistent state of low competitiveness for an extended period. Additionally, we found that the emergence of complex patterns in the model can be attributed to a specific arrangement of cells within the box, and we developed a mathematical framework that accurately describes the dynamics of the game. This framework involves a system of partial differential equations that account for the fluctuations in cell populations and influences of random choice mechanisms.

Investigating the effects of electron correlation and lattice distortions is crucial to understanding highly correlated electron systems. We have performed a detailed analysis of cupricite CuFe2S3 using a combination of first-principles calculations and a theoretical model, considering the impact of electron correlation and orbital mixing on cuprate materials. Our findings indicate that introducing sufficient electron correlation into Fe 3d orbitals leads to the separation of the bands around 2 eV, resulting in isolated Fe 4+ ions and allowing us to study the electronic properties of 3+ and 2+ ions at the 2 eV level. At the 2 eV level, corresponding to optimal doping, we have identified strong Hund's rule coupling within the Fe 3d orbitals, which causes the spectral weight to be transferred from the intermediate and high-energy regions to the low-energy region, and becomes unfavorable due to large rotational anisotropy and crystal-field splitting. This leads to the weakening of the Hund's rule coupling below 300 K, as seen in low-temperature spectral weight transfer, spin susceptibility, and magnetic susceptibility experiments. Our research also highlights the importance of orbital mixing in modifying the Hund's rule coupling and suggests strategies for increasing this effect in other 4f and 5d systems, heavily influenced by Fe 3d orbitals.

A novel approach to gigantic Rabi oscillations in solids is made possible by coupling a mobile, external excitation to a localized, hidden exciton with high magnetic moment. This enormous effect is predicted to occur in a specific, two-dimensional material structure, where Rabi oscillations are unexpectedly maximized when there is no external magnetic field. This phenomenon occurs due to a unique, internal magnetic field created by a close proximity of electrons within the hidden exciton system, which significantly increases the Rabi frequency. This result was verified through a direct observation of a Rabi oscillation cycle in a specific, isolated system. It is also shown that this effect can be utilized to develop highly efficient, magnetic-field-free systems for manipulating Rabi oscillations.

Our investigation reveals a novel, adjustable Dirac cone in a 2D electronic structure, which is based on a lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group. We explain the unique, freestanding Dirac cone, which appears twice in the irreducible Brillouin zone, arises due to the combination of two equivalent, shear-like transformations in the lattice structure. We propose that this phenomenon can be observed in a doped, 2D buckled herringbone lattice with mutually perpendicular strains, without the need for lattice shear. We theoretically examine the electronic and optical properties of this adjustable structure and demonstrate that it is possible to experimentally realize this phenomenon with current technology.

Quantum states of the field, particularly those known as single-photon facilitated coherent states, can be generated using quantum-optical catalysis with the assistance of a beam splitter. This process allows for the creation of a wide range of states that exhibit non-Gaussian behavior and are beneficial for various applications, including metrology and quantum communication systems. We demonstrate that, with the help of a beam splitter, we can successfully produce facilitated coherent states through the interaction of a pump laser and a resonator containing a single-photon device, even in the presence of photon loss. We also show that these states exhibit exemplary single-photon emissions that outperform the conventional coherent states, and this enhancement can be understood through the displacement of the ground state. Furthermore, we analyze the facilitated coherent states that can be generated with quantum-optical catalysis in both lossy and lossless environments.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the electromagnetic field and other multi-vector quantities like the conformal curvature tensor, particularly the Weyl tensor. This analysis begins by establishing the relationship between electromagnetic field coefficients and the coefficients of the Weyl tensor, before constructing the Weyl tensor from a bivector related to the electromagnetic field. We also explore conformally flat manifolds, examining how a bivector-related Weyl tensor can be expressed in terms of the conformally flat bivector and its derivatives, before discussing potential applications of this approach to gravitational field analysis.

A new technique has been introduced for generating sequence-based combinatorial libraries, specifically tailored for targeting protein-ligand interactions. This technique combines traditional linear regression with an integer optimization method to select optimal polymer sequences from a predetermined set of possible monomers. Unlike widespread machine learning approaches that focus on predicting scores rather than specific molecular structures, this technique ensures final library members conform to established chemical property criteria, such as molecular weight and polarity. Furthermore, it allows for precise control over sequence diversity and includes variables to prioritize specific amino acid distributions within the polymers. The effectiveness of this technique is illustrated through its application to a real-world example, where it successfully produces meaningful polymer libraries aimed at binding to the p53 protein.

Optimizing continuous processes in real-time through the best possible solution is a challenging control problem. This paper introduces an approach to address this issue by dividing the problem into two parts. Firstly, the process is operated at maximum efficiency for a short period of time. This efficient performance is then maintained by adjusting the variables within a wider acceptable range. We refer to this approach as performance-enhancing by transference. A specific case study involves developing a system to deliver synchronized breathing treatments for two patients with different needs. Due to the shortage of oxygen supply, delivering oxygen to both patients through the same system presented a technological barrier. We applied the direct transcription method to overcome this challenge, resulting in the development of an innovative breathing system. This project not only provides a solution to the breathing treatment shortage during the COVID-19 pandemic but also offers a platform for testing and verifying the performance-enhancing by transference approach through a breathing system testbed.

Early detection of esophageal cancer is crucial, and precise identification of tumors in CT images is vital for this purpose. While expert radiologists can accurately detect tumors by analyzing these images, their skills cannot be replicated easily. Furthermore, a significant proportion of cancer cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage, at which point treatment is ineffective. Presently available automated detection methods fall short of human expert performance. To address this challenge, we propose a novel, high-performance algorithm based on deep learning, which we refer to as the Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet). This cutting-edge network incorporates two innovative elements: firstly, the use of dilated dense blocks in a modified dense block architecture, which enhances spatial information coordination and non-linear feature interaction; secondly, an attention mechanism that facilitates coordinated multi-scale information, thereby supplementing existing cascade residual learning frameworks. The DDAUnet architecture yielded outstanding results in our experiments, outperforming a range of state-of-the-art baseline models, including the well-known UNet, atrous spatial pyramid permutation-invariant network, and dense block-based models.

The geosteering technique is utilized by EOR and increased oil recovery projects as it enables real-time decision making during well placement.  However, taking informed decisions in real-time requires the combination of collective knowledge from experts and experienced engineers along with the assessment of uncertainty from drilling data and logs.  This process is accomplished through a method called the Knowledge Tool, which is a web-based platform offering a range of functions, including data sharing, discussion forums, and decision support tools.  The Knowledge Tool is composed of several modules, including risk assessment, performance prediction, and placement recommendations.  These modules are built using statistical models and incorporate uncertainty estimates derived from historical data.  During operation, these models are updated with data from the current well placement session.  The application of the Knowledge Tool is illustrated through its use in a real-world geosteering project in a heavy oil reservoir.  The results showed that combining the expertise of a team of engineers with the data from the well led to adjustments to the drilling trajectory that significantly improved the likelihood of the well's successful production.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on NER with overlapping entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which fail to capture the holistic structure of sentences. In contrast, this study introduces a novel method to integrate named entity identification with sentence structure parsing to address the limitations of these models. By representing a sentence as a graph and introducing a new type of bi-lateral bi-affinity parser, this approach enables the simultaneous identification and parsing of sentence structures. Our experiments show that this method outperforms the state-of-the-art linear models and achieves particularly impressive results on the Japanese NER dataset.

We present a method to count the number of bitangents to a smooth surface of degree 4 in $\mathbb{P}^2$, in a manner that is both rational and computationally efficient. This approach enables a detailed examination of the symmetries present in this collection of curves, including those related to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-action that preserves the set of bitangents. A precise count of the curves obtained by applying this $\mathbb{A}^1$-action to a specific element is also provided, along with an examination of their real signed tally.

The surge in IoT applications is creating significant demand for accurate device localization. One method to achieve this using localization is through wireless sensor networks, which provide real-time location finding. In our research, we concentrate on finding the location of moving objects within 3D space using time difference of arrival (TDOA) and received signal strength (RSS). Our investigation considers external interference affecting measurement variability, which hinders location detection. To address this challenge, we develop and evaluate two approaches - a method using maximum likelihood estimation and another using a hyper-ellipse model - to determine the position of a target with minimal error, which is supported by experimental data.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current challenges and potential factors influencing the development of natural language processing algorithms for code-mixed content, particularly for communities speaking multiple languages.

Human references are commonly used to evaluate the accuracy of automatic image descriptions, but concerns have been raised regarding the reliability of this method. This risk is heightened in controlled studies. A survey-based evaluation method is proposed that utilizes human references in a more authentic setting. In this approach, the evaluation of image description systems is subject to individual variability, but it is believed that group trends would still accurately reflect system performance. A practical application of this proposal is included, involving the assessment of two current state-of-the-art models for generating image descriptions.

Tantalum oxide with the highest concentration of oxygen, Ta$_2$O$_5$, has been extensively investigated for its exceptional electrical, mechanical, and optical properties; moreover, it has significant potential in microelectronic applications and as a wear-resistant coating. Despite these intriguing features, a fundamental aspect of Ta$_2$O_5 has yet to be fully understood – its crystal base structure. Recent studies have proposed variants of the orthorhombic system with similar dimensions, however, they have not been consistently validated, and there is a lack of clear agreement on the effects of different crystal system variations on the physical characteristics of Ta$_2$O_5. In this research, we have integrated density functional theory simulations with a Monte Carlo method to thoroughly examine the possible variants of Ta$_2$O_5 polymorphs and investigate their energetic stability under different pressure conditions. Our results reveal that Ta$_2$O_5 has the highest stability in the monoclinic system at ambient pressure, and this stability is conversely affected by increased pressure, which favors the orthorhombic system. Our findings also dispel the misconception that Ta$_2$O_5 has a complex electronic structure; instead, we found that its conductivity can be metal, semiconductor, or insulating, depending on the pressure and system variation. This research provides a comprehensive understanding of the Ta$_2$O_5 structure, which can be further applied to studying the material's physical characteristics and

The concept of the Big Sort refers to the phenomenon described by Joseph H. Nye, where like-minded individuals are drawn to the same locations, leading to the polarization of communities. This paper explores the implications of this geographic sorting on the dissemination of misinformation within American Reddit users. Utilizing online user data and a dataset of false information, we examine how the spread of misinformation is affected by the level of polarization in communities. Our findings indicate that highly polarized communities are more likely to have misinformation disseminated to them, as confirmed by subsequent fact-checking. The efficiency of misinformation dissemination is further increased when communities are composed of highly similar individuals. These outcomes are consistent with the principles of the Big Sort, as they are influenced by the degree of polarization present and the homogeneous nature of the community.

We aim to detect anomalies in real-time, high-volume, and continuous data streams, which are characteristic of modern information systems. Our approach focuses on discovering unusual patterns within these systems by leveraging the power of distributed computing and stream processing. By leveraging the past behavior of programs and their underlying data, we can identify deviations from established expectations and detect potential security breaches and performance issues. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by applying it to a variety of use cases, including analyzing database query logs and detecting DDoS attacks, which we evaluate using a parallel processing framework and a cloud-based DDoS detection system.

Instructors use spoken language to teach students about a task's details, which is not necessarily evident from mere visual observations of the task. Understanding this aspect of teaching is crucial for developing effective learning methods that can grasp the underlying logic of a task. Currently, there is a lack of research focusing on the auditory component of teaching, particularly on how speakers convey essential information through speech when demonstrating a task to others. This study investigates speech patterns of human instructors while they demonstrate manipulation skills to a robot. We collect and analyze a dataset that includes speech, corresponding action sequences and the instructors' spoken language. Our analysis reveals a range of speech patterns associated with action sequences and often present in various configurations, which we term "acoustic action programs". We also present a method to automatically identify these patterns and validate its effectiveness through multiple tests. This research may contribute to the development of more efficient learning methods that can effectively utilize spoken instructions when taught by humans.

Building on previous work, we propose an approach to randomly generating ordered trees of any degree, based on a generating function introduced by Bonna, Clerc and Dulieu. Our method is grounded in the underlying exponential family of distributions and is therefore minimax efficient. We derive an indirect formula for computing the moments of the number of nodes in a randomly generated tree, as well as a direct formula that enables us to develop a direct simulation method. We illustrate our results with an examination of a specific example.

Euler-Arnold equations have far-reaching implications as they underpin sophisticated mathematical structures, including bihamiltonian systems, integrable deformations, and certain infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian challenges. This paper delves into the relationship between these esteemed equations and conformal field theories, specifically identifying key factors that contribute to the complexity of such theories. We also present novel, quasihamiltonian approaches in both 2D and higher-dimensional conformal field theories, and our findings suggest that these methods yield new insights into the challenging issue of conformal field theory genus zero constraints.

The growing popularity of conversational interfaces, such as chatbots and virtual assistants, has created a significant need for a more effective and efficient method of testing these systems. Traditional manual evaluation methods have become inadequate due to the high cost and time-consuming process of gathering accurate, detailed information on how the systems are performing. A more viable solution is a machine-based testing system that utilizes a combination of natural language processing and learning algorithms to simulate a normal user interaction with the system. This approach enables the rapid development of multiple scenarios from a small initial dataset and significantly reduces the time and expense associated with traditional testing methods. This paper will provide an overview of the principles underlying this type of testing and the specific algorithm used in our machine testing system. We will also present the results of a case study that compares our method to established evaluation techniques.

The existence of an unknown celestial body in the outer reaches of our solar system has long been hypothesized based on the orbital patterns of the known Solar system bodies.  Object X, also referred to as the Solar system's 'ninth planet', is believed to have mass sufficient to cause a significant gravitational effect on nearby celestial bodies in their orbits.  Given its hypothesized mass and orbital distance, it's possible that Object X could have a notable effect on the orbital patterns of the inner and outer planets, particularly those with the highest eccentricity.  In the present study, the gravitational influence of Object X is modeled and compared to the actual and predicted celestial body trajectories as calculated using the two-body and n-body gravitational models.  Based on these calculations, it can be seen that the existing tracking data of the inner and outer planets is not sufficient to confirm the existence of Object X as the existing data fits equally well with both models.  However, it's also found that the best fit to the actual trajectories occurs when the model includes a relatively low orbital eccentricity for Object X, which could have implications for its discoverability through very long period planetary alignments.

The neural machine translation model's lack of interpretability hinders understanding its intricate decision-making process. To circumvent this issue, we propose a novel framework that incorporates a neural machine translation model as a neural machine interpretation model, where the model is trained to mimic the translation process. By leveraging the translated text along with the original input, our framework can pinpoint the vital segments of the input that influence the translation output. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by achieving notable performance improvements and providing visually stimulating examples using a state-of-the-art neural machine translation model on two diverse test sets.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, known as Conformal Cyclic Cosmology markers, could provide evidence for a theoretical framework based on General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics. These patterns would arise from an earlier cosmic era and offer a window into the past through the laws of thermodynamics. In the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model, the universe undergoes a cycle of expansion and contraction, with temperatures above the Grand Unified Theory's unification point playing a crucial role. The possibility of detecting these patterns in the CMB has been explored through statistical analysis of temperature fluctuations in the Planck and WMAP datasets. In addition, a public database containing 10,000 possible configurations of the multiverse has been used in conjunction with the BICEP3 experiment's dataset to identify potential anomalies in the CMB. Results from these analyses suggest that the universe exhibits spatial symmetry and contains geometric structures such as Calabi-Yau manifolds. The discovery of Conformal Cyclic Cosmology markers in the CMB would have significant implications for our understanding of the universe, potentially revealing the presence of the multiverse and the effects of Quantum Gravity.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing an Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by showing that when the initial data satisfies a certain Harnack inequality condition, the Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature has strong convergence properties, ultimately yielding a smooth and long-lasting solution. The condition in question is met by the trivial solution, as well as solutions derived from the flow starting from data within a specific H\"older class category. The paper also includes a discussion on potential infinity-time regularity results for these types of equations.

Deep neural networks have historically excelled in object recognition tasks, yet they struggle when presented with novel classes using only a limited number of samples. This paper proposes an innovative approach that addresses this challenge by allowing the network to learn generalizations about the underlying categories from a small number of examples. Unlike previous methods that focus on learning a single representation for all categories at once, our approach enables the discovery of unique prototypes specific to each class. By constraining the number of prototypes and employing a prototype-extraction module, our network effectively generalizes to new classes from a limited amount of data. We evaluate our method's generalization capabilities to new classes using the mini-ImageNet and few-shot iNat datasets, and our results indicate that it surpasses previous state-of-the-art approaches in the few-shot learning setting.

Cross-domain and multi-sparse-domain recommender systems have become increasingly popular as they offer personalized suggestions by integrating information from multiple platforms. Although various approaches have been proposed, significant challenges remain in handling multiple sparse domains with distinct item types. In response to this issue, our research introduces a novel technique called the Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation model (MSDCR), which leverages a neural network to increase user connection scores across all domains and provide personalized item recommendations based on a unified attribute preference learning framework. By enhancing user connections and preserving original ordering, the MSDCR outperforms existing methods in multi-sparse-domain cross-domain recommendation tasks and is particularly effective in supporting real-world online cross-domain and multi-sparse-domain recommendation applications. In particular, it is now feasible to accurately predict long-tail items in multiple sparse domains across different platforms. The source code and the dataset for the MSDCR are available at this link https://github.com/zwang84/MSDCR, which serves as an example of a state-of-the-art multi-sparse-domain cross-domain recommendation framework.

Convex optimization issues often employ second-order cone constraints, which can also be represented using conic formulations over other convex cones such as rotated second-order cones and their variants. While many conic solvers can handle these standard cones, some problems require the use of non-standard cones that can only be solved with customized conic solvers. We present Hypatia, a Julia package that can convert a problem with these custom cones into a equivalent problem using standard cones, allowing it to be solved with any Julia convex optimization solver that supports conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality assessment to ensure reliability and accuracy in subsequent analyses. Although deep learning-based approaches have succeeded in predicting MRI quality, they are limited by their inability to understand the underlying causes of predicted outcomes. This study deviates from focusing solely on prediction and instead seeks to present a more comprehensive understanding, as it is crucial to comprehend how to accurately assess MRI quality across various settings. By collecting and analyzng a vast dataset consisting of 200,000+ MRI images alongside their corresponding quality labels and acquisition details, our analysis revealed a complex pattern of relationships between these factors and predicted outcomes and demonstrated the effectiveness of utilizing a generalizable model for assessing MRI quality, as desired by healthcare providers and researchers. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of "quality-aware" training, adjusting the model's performance based on the provider's preferences, which significantly improves prediction accuracy (+2.5%) and achieves comparable results with traditional approaches using a more limited dataset (+6.5%).

The rising number of privately owned electric vehicles presents a significant challenge for distribution network management due to their impact on network resilience and efficiency. Utilizing a multi-agent optimization framework in a simulated environment, we evaluate the effects of privately owned electric cars on distribution network resilience and investigate optimal coordination strategies between network operators and drivers. The results show that coordinated action can reduce the risk of network failure by as much as 50% and decrease average repair time by 38%. The most effective coordination strategies depend on various factors, including the location of drivers and the status of network components. Further research is needed to address practical implementation challenges and potential security issues arising from the integration of driver agents with the distribution network.

This performance evaluation provides hands-on data and insight into the capabilities of the Intel Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) when integrated with the Linux kernel 4.15 and the Ubuntu 18.04 LTS operating system. By harnessing the power of next-generation storage technology, applications with high memory-to-persistent storage access patterns can experience significant performance gains. The Intel Optane DC PMM offers an attractive and high-performance alternative to traditional solid-state drives, suitable for demanding workloads and applications that can take advantage of its unique persistent memory capabilities.

In collaborative scenarios, agents may choose to hold meetings to achieve shared goals, potentially involving coordination and strategic decision-making. We introduce a novel framework of persistent, co-located agents that can decide whether to meet, separate from traditional approaches to cooperative learning. Our investigation into this dynamic of persistent meeting and departure leads to the development of a DRIVE system. This system effectively learns the agents' behavior in response to their environment and fellow agents, allowing it to make informed decisions about whether to attend meetings based on expected outcomes. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through laboratory testing and analysis of its components.

We employed a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method to
systematically investigate the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of
Gd/Cladlan and GdCladlan Sn$_3$ compounds. The calculations were performed under
pressure conditions ranging from 0 to 20 GPa. The results indicate that both
Gd and Cm based compounds crystallize in the AuCu$_3$ structure and exhibit a
metallic nature with significant covalent bonding. Under increased pressure, the
volume reduction leads to a phase transition from a metal to a half-metal in the
GdSn$_3$ compound, whereas the CmSn$_3$ compound remains metallic across the
studied pressure range. Interestingly, the CmSn$_3$ compound displays a
non-trivial spin-orbit-induced topological insulator characteristic only at
zero GPa, in contrast to the GdSn$_3$ compound which exhibits a pressure
induced non-trivial topological phase transition. Furthermore, our findings
also indicate that the half-metallic and topological properties of these
compounds can be controlled by applying external pressure.

Lattice QCD calculations allow for the prediction of physical properties of hadrons through the calculation of hadron correlation functions. By applying Monte Carlo integration and the maximum likelihood method to these correlations, we can estimate the parameters of quark and meson spectra. A statistical framework is presented for accurately determining the masses of exotic hadrons, baryons, and mesons, as well as mixtures of quark states, within a specific system and mass range. The method is demonstrated using a lattice configuration of end-points spanning a range of 0 to 2 in the quark axis and a 0 to 1.5 range in the meson axis.
Building on earlier work by Fomin and Lytton, we generalize their foundation theorem to the infinite family of reflection arrays known as the generalized finite Coxeter graphs of type B.

Using the Pantheon sample of 460 Type Ia Supernovae, a relationship between the light curve shape and luminosity has been confirmed and a correction has been applied to account for lensing effects. By analyzing the data with a focus on cosmological constants, a first constraint on the lensing parameter sigma_v = 116 +/- 65 km^2, with a 95% confidence level, has been obtained. This analysis assumes a Hubble constant of 69.2 km^2 Mpc^-3.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations given at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021.  The course was presented via the Zoom videoconferencing system to participants from the University of Oxford, Imperial College London and the African Institute in Tanzania.  The notes are aimed at graduate students and research workers in the fields of analysis, stochastic processes and partial differential equations.  The lectures introduced the main concepts of a wide range of SPDEs, covering existence and uniqueness of solutions, the method of fractional integrals and derivatives, stochastic evolution equations, parabolic equations with rough noise, stochastic differential equations in abstract Wiener spaces and the fourth order Allen-Cahn equation.

In this analysis, a novel type of point defect, which we call T hub, is identified in the photonic silicon-on-insulator system. It is shown that this defect has unique characteristics, exhibiting both a defect mode associated with a Hubbard site and a mode linked to a T site within a one-dimensional sublattice. The conditions required for the defect mode to behave like a Hubbard or T site model are determined and demonstrated with an example of a T hub used in a quantum simulation of a mixed-valence Hubbard model.

This study investigates the use of MRI imaging and machine learning to diagnose breast cancer, a leading cause of death among women globally. If left untreated, cancer can spread and prove fatal. Advanced medical technologies such as MRI scans have improved early detection rates. However, accurately diagnosing cancer in MRI images remains a challenging task. Radiologists may misdiagnose or miss tumors during routine examinations, highlighting the need for reliable and efficient tumor detection methods. This research explores the application of machine learning in tumor detection. Initially, four different feature extraction techniques were compared to enhance the quality of MRI images. The experiments revealed that the technique produces the highest accuracy of 97.5%. A model incorporating was used to detect tumors in MRI images, yielding an accuracy of 97.5%. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of machine learning in tumor detection and the superiority of over other methods.

We present a novel algebraic approach in identifying hidden characteristics of irrational numbers that, when raised to a specific power, result in rational outcomes. Specifically, we establish an algebraic relationship that distinguishes certain algebraic subfields within the real numbers from their counterparts in the complex numbers. Building upon this discovery, we develop an algebraic method to identify and characterize a specific subset of algebraic and non-algebraic numbers, including those related to the minimal polynomial of the complex nth roots of unity. Moreover, this method enables us to derive an algebraic formula for identifying when the nth root of a given number is an algebraic number, and provide an algebraic proof for the non-algebraic nature of certain numbers, including the square root of 2 and the golden ratio.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs make their spectra unsuitable for most spectroscopic analysis techniques that rely on line invariability. One approach to address this issue is the line selection method for least-squares deconvolution, which identifies a subset of lines resistant to stellar activity and other external distortions. We examined two diverse line sets, one comprehensive and another random, to determine if they yield comparable results for a case study involving the M dwarf M8. We utilized the ARES line catalog extensively in our analysis. When testing the sensitivity of the line selection method, we discovered that while the line sets performed similarly in terms of resisting external distortions and varying stellar activity, the line selection based on a comprehensive catalog showed lesser residual scatter when compared to a random selection. This difference in performance was further shown to be influenced by the line's virtual equivalent width. Both line sets demonstrated the ability to accurately determine key atmospheric parameters and deliver reliable mass-radius predictions for planets around M dwarfs.

This research paper proposes an innovative approach, 'HSSBPE,' to optimize data collection processes in Wireless Sensor Networks. We address two key challenges in such networks: the complex 'capture problem' and inefficient 'communication overhead.' The HSSBPE approach is designed to mitigate these issues through the use of a hierarchical network structure and bidirectional link quality assessment. We compare HSSBPE to existing hierarchical and non-hierarchical protocols and demonstrate that HSSBPE achieves better results in terms of network efficiency and communication overhead in scenarios where a large number of sensors come together to report critical events.

When using deep neural networks for object recognition, the effect of external context becomes a significant consideration. This study undertakes a comprehensive analysis to understand how context influences these networks. Initially, we examine if the presence of context (such as surrounding objects) affects the accuracy of these networks. This analysis is conducted across three scenarios: (1) involving diverse objects in a variety of configurations, (2) focusing on relationships between pairs of objects, and (3) exploring how networks perform in different contextual settings. Our investigation involves using a range of contextual patterns and testing the robustness of our findings against different dataset splits. Our findings are also verified using additional evaluation methods. This research provides valuable insights for practitioners working with deep neural networks and offers key adjustments that can be made to improve the performance of these networks in real-world applications.

We establish a concentration inequality for a set of binary random variables whose mutual information meets a specific 'anti-correlation' criterion. Additionally, an inequality relating the partial entropies of these variables is also proven, which has implications for his goal. Furthermore, our results are demonstrated on two particular scenarios.

We establish a relative Fontaine-Tate theory for Breuil-Kato-Chai's rigidity module over the power series ring $A_{\text{inf}}$ in variables $p$ and $x$. This builds upon previous work by Kato, Breuil-Kato-Chai, and Pollack, and leads to a relative Fontaine-Tate theory for modules of characteristic $p>2$ within the context of p-adic geometry.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. We demonstrate that the interference term between the helicity non-zero amplitude and the helicity zero amplitude leads to a specific angle dependence, namely cosphi_R, in hadron production, primarily influenced by the interference between the twist-2 quark helicity distribution and the twist-3 quark vector parton distribution. Our calculations reveal that the interference term's contribution dominates the asymmetry at moderate x values, whereas the cosphi_R dependence in hadron production is dominated by the helicity distribution at high x values. Furthermore, the interference term becomes negative for mid-momentum hadron production and becomes more significant with increasing Q values.

We resolve the ambiguity in Fock's coordinate transformation by choosing the conventional unitary operator over the alternative one, which results in the emergence of a cosmological constant in the de Sitter space. Furthermore, this interpretation leads to the establishment of a one-to-one correspondence between the Fock coordinates and the standard de Sitter coordinates, ultimately revealing that the de Sitter space is inherently endowed with a non-local feature.

We maintain that a symplectic manifold can be modified through a minor adjustment to become a closed symplectic manifold with the same volume. Additionally, this alteration can be performed in a way that is geodesic-compatible, resulting in a closed geodesic surface with the same volume and curvature. Furthermore, this technique can be extended to a broader category of manifolds with boundary.

We called this paper, because it has no citation. Wikipedia's vast information base allows it to recommend relevant entities to user queries. Wikipedia's categorization provides valuable context for entity recommendations. In this paper, we propose a technique to leverage Wikipedia's categorization for entity suggestions. Our approach uses a layered Wikipedia knowledge base to provide recommendations. This base is made up of categories of entities, where each entity then belongs to multiple categories. When a user searches for entities, our system recommends the ones that match the search query and also fit the categories associated with the search. We tested this approach on the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph, and found that it significantly improves entity recommendations over a plain graph method.

The success of kidney transplantation is heavily dependent on the availability of compatible kidneys. Unfortunately, many potential donors are ruled out due to incompatible blood types, antibodies, or other factors. In some cases, living donors with incompatible recipients may consider donating a kidney that could be accepted through desensitization treatments. To better understand this complex situation, we develop a mathematical framework to analyze the decisions made by potential donors. Our model is particularly useful in evaluating the outcomes of two common desensitization approaches, the T-cell amputation protocol and the kidney paired donation method. We examine how the probability of rejection affects these outcomes and facilitates comparisons between the two desensitization methods. Moreover, we establish conditions under which one approach yields a higher success rate than the other. Our findings also provide insights for policymakers seeking to develop strategies to increase the acceptance of incompatible kidneys.

The concept of implicit models has been a thriving area in machine learning, enabling the efficient processing of large-scale datasets by training low-dimensional representations. In the context of implicit deep learning models, particularly those using explicit functional transformations, the input data is transformed through a series of nested functions. This typically occurs in models based on implicit differentiable hash functions and neural collaborative filtering, which have shown significant advantages over their non-implicit counterparts in terms of computational efficiency and memory requirements. Despite their success, these models pose difficulties for conventional optimization methods due to the absence of an explicit form for the mapping function. To address this challenge, researchers have developed an alternative approach based on optimizing an explicitly defined mapping function through the use of auxiliary neural network variables. This has led to further developments in both the area of implicit modeling and optimization methods.

This paper undertakes an in-depth analysis of the previous studies using word representations and machine learning algorithms to predict Loughran-McDonald's text word polarities. We examine various embedding models, including classic matrix representations of words and advanced neural network-based models. We assess these representations in a supervised learning framework, utilizing part-of-speech tags as an intermediate variable to improve predictive accuracy. Our findings show that several modern embedding models outperform previous methods and suggest improvements to the Loughran-McDonald Sentiment Word Lists. We also find that the relationships between words and their polarities are not as rigidly defined as previously thought, and therefore, these lists should be updated from a linguistic perspective. We make available our code and a dataset of sentiment-inferenced word polarities, along with models, at our website.

This paper proposes a technique that simultaneously conveys information and transfers energy to multiple receivers using an OFDM system with a single information-carrying and multiple energy-transferring antennas. As the number of receiving antennas approaches the number of subcarriers, a MISO-OFDM system can be seen as a close approximation. Moreover, we demonstrate that by optimizing a function that considers both information transmission and energy transfer, our SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems experience an increase of up to 10.3 and 9.4 dB, respectively, in the energy transfer rate over a vast bandwidth, compared to a system where the information and energy transfer are separated. Additionally, these systems provide a higher data transfer rate and a higher energy transfer rate, with only a minor increase in the receiver's signal processing complexity.

This research introduces a hybrid approach that combines level-set and embedded boundary methods to model the interaction of fluids with changing phase. The level-set technique was adapted to handle interface resolution and fluid fluid dynamics, while the embedded boundary approach was used to handle fluid-solid interactions, particularly focusing on the removal of singularity at phase change interfaces. A numerical algorithm was developed to solve the resulting equations, and its performance was tested with notable problems involving melting, solidification, and Stefan problems.

Classic logical systems featuring unary operators are viewed from an abstract algebra perspective as distributive lattices, with modalities representing functions distributing over arbitrary set operations. This conventional approach fails to capture the unique properties inherent to unary modalities in language, as seen through the lens of categorial grammar and type systems. A distinct, twisted interpretation of distributive lattices is introduced, which aligns unary modalities with context-dependent functions that selectively apply to atomic statements, thus providing an abstract algebra framework compatible with the underlying structure of language as described through type systems and categorial grammar.

We take a comprehensive approach to addressing a widespread challenge in designing multiplayer online competitions: identifying rationalizable equilibria. Our solution framework automatically generates an equilibrium in which all players act in accordance with computationally efficient, self-serving rules, ensuring that no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally deviating. To facilitate efficient computation, we introduce a novel algorithm that leverages a coarsely grained representation of payoff functions, reducing the required communication between players and the necessary computation. We showcase the effectiveness of our method in various scenarios, including applications to online auctions, mechanism design, and the development of self-stabilizing protocols.

The issue of epidemic spreading on wireless sensor networks has been considered in this research. We examine two scenarios: the S-A model, where active sensors spread the epidemic, and the S-O model, where sensors in both active and dormant states can be infected. A key feature of these systems is the ability to dynamically switch between different numbers of active sensors based on system conditions. This ability is referred to as preventive overload redistribution. We investigate the effects of this feature on the spread of epidemics, analyzing both models and providing solutions that leverage preventive overload redistribution to reduce epidemic outbreaks. In the S-A model, we identify the critical threshold that determines whether an epidemic spreads, and in the S-O model, we determine the conditions under which the epidemic is controlled using analytic and simulation methods.

In this study, we examine Cotton solitons within the context of nearly Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds.
